title: Atomic Emission Spectra
learning_goal: Investigate atomic emission spectra and connect spectral lines to electromagnetic radiation and atomic energy levels.

stages.title: 1. Atoms emit specific wavelengths
stages.content: Excited atoms can emit electromagnetic radiation at specific wavelengths rather than every possible wavelength.

stages.title: 2. Energy levels
stages.content: Electrons in atoms occupy quantized energy levels. When an electron moves from a higher level to a lower level, the atom emits a photon with energy equal to the energy difference.

stages.title: 3. Spectral fingerprints
stages.content: Each element has a characteristic pattern of emission lines because each element has its own allowed energy levels.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: Hydrogen produces a distinct set of visible spectral lines. Those lines correspond to specific electron transitions and therefore specific photon energies.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Why can an emission spectrum be used to identify an unknown element?
stages.hint: Think about whether different elements have identical or unique energy-level patterns.
stages.alternate_explanation: The spectral-line pattern acts like a fingerprint because each element has a unique set of allowed electron transitions.
stages.answer: Because each element has a characteristic set of emission lines.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, explain why atomic spectra are discrete, connect photon emission to electron transitions, and describe how spectra identify elements.
